who_for: A robot vacuum is best for keeping floors consistently clean between deeper cleanings, especially with pets or a busy household. It won't replace a stick or upright vacuum for stairs, upholstery, or tight corners.
Self-emptying docks are worth the extra cost if you don't want to empty a small bin every day or two. Mopping models make the most sense in homes with a lot of hard flooring.

how_we_picked.label: Navigation
how_we_picked.text: Lidar and camera-based mapping lets a robot clean in neat rows, avoid obstacles, and respect no-go zones. We passed over models that bump around at random.

how_we_picked.label: Pickup on carpet and hair
how_we_picked.text: Suction numbers alone can mislead, so we also weighed brush design and tangle resistance, which matter most for pet hair.

how_we_picked.label: Dock and maintenance
how_we_picked.text: We compared self-empty bag capacity, mop washing and drying, and the ongoing cost of replacement bags and pads.

how_we_picked.label: App and obstacle avoidance
how_we_picked.text: Reliable avoidance of cords and socks, plus a clear app with room-by-room control, separates good robots from frustrating ones.

how_we_picked.label: Noise and battery
how_we_picked.text: We looked at runtime relative to home size and how loud each robot is on its standard setting.
